messages.text: Monday, November 16 · Canton, Michigan
Tuba resonance in Ann Arbor and the quiet drift of herbicide research

An overcast Sunday brings a cool, steady temperature perfect for indoor academic seminars or evening recitals. Local attention turns to the intersection of environmental impact studies and regional legal developments.
Expect overcast skies throughout the day with a high near 50 degrees and a low of 35 degrees.
The sun rises at 7:26 AM and sets at 5:11 PM, with the moon currently in its first-quarter phase at 38.3 percent illumination.
Academic and musical rhythms
Consider the lecture on boundary stratifications of Hurwitz spaces at East Hall at 4:00 PM. Later, Jake Alford performs a tuba recital at the Walgreen Drama Center at 8:00 PM.
A community meeting is scheduled for November 18 at 6:30 PM.
Legal filings and environmental research

Osama Siblani has filed a defamation lawsuit against former U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers in Wayne County Circuit Court. Meanwhile, University of Michigan research highlights that low doses of the herbicide dicamba cause wood sorrel to produce smaller, more numerous flowers.
Looking toward the week
Prepare for the 862 Meeting taking place this Tuesday evening.

Tuesday, November 17 · Canton, Michigan
Leonids under overcast skies and the fortune of Polish tradition

A quiet, overcast Monday settles over Canton as meteor showers grace the sky and local cultural traditions offer a warm indoor escape. We track the intersection of celestial movement and the community's rhythm.
Expect an overcast day with a high near 55 degrees and a low around 30 degrees.
The sun rises at 7:27 AM and sets at 5:10 PM, with the moon in its first-quarter phase at 47.8 percent illumination.
A Monday for tradition
Experience the Polish tradition of Andrzejki at Haven Hall in Ann Arbor at 11:00 AM for an afternoon of fortune-telling and festive games.
The community gathers for the 862 Meeting tomorrow, November 18, at 6:30 PM.
Crisis response and local faculty concerns

Ann Arbor has officially launched the A2 REACH crisis response team to pair police officers with social workers for mental health support. Meanwhile, the University of Michigan Faculty Senate recently issued a vote of no confidence regarding police and labor negotiations.
Looking toward the end of the week
Mark your calendar for the Girls Gear Up outreach event taking place on November 21 at 7:30 AM.
